chapter: Uptown clubs and the Black Cat
title: The Exclusive Club and working with Willie Gant
summary: He moved with Simmons to the Exclusive Club and played in a duo with stride pianist Willie Gant.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, now -- the Yeah Man -- what -- wait a minute -- where was this 101 One on One Ranch? When does that come in?
The 101 One on One --
Didn't you say you played there?
No, no, no. I used to go there.
Oh. You used to go there. Okay.
Yeah.
Now where did you say you went from Yeah Man? You and Lonnie went to where?
A place called The Exclusive club.
Yeah. Was that the same type of a club?
Same type.
And by now you're on guitar?
Yes.
Yeah.
And, I'm playing opposite Willie Gant,
I've never heard of him.
Never heard of him?
Never heard of him.
Oh, Willie Gant, Willie Gant and the Blue Lambert When they used to talk about Blue Lambert.
Yeah. Well, he must really have been top notch.
Oh yeah.
Did he die a year or two ago?
Huh?
Did he -- was still around -- he died a year or two ago?
Who's that, Grant?
Yeah.
Yeah.
Not long ago.
Not long ago. Right.
Somebody, you know, I think it was was telling me he was playing over on the past side.
Yeah. He was over there for a long time.
I didn't know that. I was --
Yeah. And I wanted to get over there to hear him, you know, but I never, you know --
Yeah.
I was always out of town.
Well, I mean, was he the same class as the Lion, Fats...
Well, yeah. He was the same school. The same school.
Lucky Roberts.
Yes.
Yeah.
It was the same school of -- stride piano.
Yeah. He would be playing opposite you?
No, no, no. I'm working with him.
Oh?
Oh?
That's what I meant.
Oh.
No, I'm working with him.
Oh. Well, that was pretty -- fairly important for you?
For me -- yes. We really got along well musically, and socially
Yeah.
You know, in that sense.
Well, what about playing sort of rhythm guitar with stride piano,
It was good as far as I'm concerned,
It really does go together.
Well, I should think that's where you got it. Where you got your training, huh, Freddie?
I think so. Looking back on it now -- you know, I've never thought about that before -- until now.
I mean, because that was your big thing.
It was just the two of us.
-- Rhythm guitar player.
Just the two of you?
Just the two.
Oh?
No, no. Either didn't --. Let me see what happened to Lonnie now. I think Lonnie came over there for

a while, and then he left -- something happened to him -- and there was just two of us. I can't -- I don't remember what happened (to Lannie) during that period. But, anyway, it was just the two of us.
